paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. The wall was finished, and the first thing they did was not take a victory lap. They purified themselves, the people, the gates and the wall (Nehemiah 12:30). Before the party, they got right with God, and I think that tells you where the joy comes from.

Then comes the part I love. They rejoiced "because God had given them great joy," and "the joy of Jerusalem was heard from afar" (Nehemiah 12:43). Joy that big isn't something you work up. It's something God hands you, and it spills out of you so loud the neighbors can hear. Heard from AFAR, friend! I could barely get a squeak out of that junk drawer.

And look at what they did the same day. They put men over the storerooms so the priests and Levites were provided for, "because Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who were serving" (Nehemiah 12:44). Singers, gatekeepers, priests and people all had a part, and worship kept going long after the music stopped. So here's your takeaway, baker: thank God out loud, and then keep doing your part, every day. That's a batch worth baking, and Nehemiah's story isn't finished yet.
